correctness.rationale: An independent Cartesian Taylor expansion and exact polynomial reduction (python /workspace/branches/replay_torsion_algebra.py) reproduced the normalized torsion numerator, endpoint factorizations and decisive curvature components. Because R>1, the radial cross-product component forces sin(qt)=0 at a curvature zero; the other components exclude the outer equator and give exactly R=1+x at the inner equator. The cubic is strictly convex on [-1,1] and negative at zero. On each half interval it has one simple interior root iff the remote endpoint is positive; the signs are those of R-R_- and R_+-R respectively. The endpoint root at +1 has positive derivative in c and therefore order two in t, with nonvanishing curvature. The endpoint root at -1 is excluded even when a separate regular root survives. Each interior root gives 2q parameters and each endpoint q; coprimality ensures these are distinct points. The thresholds cannot coincide because x is rational and the crossing ratio squared is 1+sqrt(3). The argument checks all parameters analytically, not just the frozen test samples.
